tasks.task: Write a wedding speech or best man toast

items.when: When someone asks for a personal speech and you need the steps from first call to the day
When the speaker has memories but no shape, to pull out the two or three stories worth telling
When the stories and names are in, to write the speech timed to the slot
When the speaker wants a dry, funny version built on one true story, with the pauses marked
When the draft is warm but flat and needs a few sharp, true lines
When a mishap story is funny in the telling but has no point or ending yet
Before the day, when the room holds family, children, older relatives or a boss

tasks.task: Write a eulogy or memorial speech

items.when: When the family has many memories and you need the few that show who the person was
When you have the stories and names and need a eulogy that fits the service slot
When you want a second version shaped for the ear, with a line that returns
When the draft lists a life's dates and jobs but not the true details that show the person
When the draft is done, to find the lines that pull away from the feeling you meant

tasks.task: Write a conference talk or keynote around one real case

items.when: When a speaking slot is confirmed and you need the steps from notes to stage in order
When the speaker has a topic and loose notes but no single case to hang the talk on
When the case and the ask are chosen and you need the full script for a 10 to 20 minute slot
When you want a second shape to compare: two or three lessons, each with its own story
When the outline is in order of events and the room would not know the stakes until late
When the talk rambles and the audience cannot tell what it asks of them
When the script is drafted, to find the flat stretches where a room stops listening

tasks.task: Write a 60-second and a 3-minute pitch

items.when: Before the script, to set the order that builds belief and ends on one clear decision
When you need both pitch lengths with answers to the likeliest questions
When the speaker needs 10, 30 and 60 second versions and an opening question to compare
When the pitch leans on a rival's name, to try versions built on what only they do
When the first ten words are weak, to get three openers and a way to test them
When the pitch is drafted, to find the toughest objections and where it overclaims

tasks.task: Polish a speech the client already wrote

items.when: When the draft reads well on paper but was written for the eye, not the ear
When the draft tries to say everything, to name the one idea and cut what fights it
When the words are fancy and the pauses are in the wrong place
When lines trip the tongue, to find each one and fix it so it can be said in one breath
When the polish is done, to time it against the slot before the speaker rehearses

tasks.task: Write a retirement, leaving or farewell speech

items.when: When colleagues send scattered memories and you need the ones the whole room will know
When you have the stories and need a speech that thanks people by name and fits the slot
When the person leaving is the speaker and wants to pass on two or three lessons
When the office expects a roast and you want a deadpan version to compare
Before the day, to check the teasing is safe in front of a boss and junior staff

tasks.task: Write a short birthday or anniversary toast

items.when: When you have one or two stories and need a toast of two minutes or less
When the room wants a laugh, to try a version built on one story told straight-faced
When the toast needs one line people will repeat as they raise a glass
When the toast runs past two minutes and must lose words without losing the ending

tasks.task: Write an obituary or written tribute

items.when: When the family gives you dates and jobs and you need the details that made the person
When the tribute will be read, not spoken, and must fit a notice or an order of service
When the tribute has drifted into stock phrases the family would never say
Before it is printed, to catch a name, place or date spelt two ways

tasks.task: Script an investor pitch

items.when: Before the script, to plan the order of belief and the decision you ask investors for
When the founder needs spoken scripts from one minute to ten, with likely questions
When the pitch says "like X but", to compare versions that stand without a rival
When the script is drafted, to have it grilled by tough investors before the real room
When there are slides, to check slide count, talk time and type size against the slot
When the pitch states numbers, to back each claim with a dated source and list the gaps

tasks.task: Revise a pitch after feedback or a no

items.when: When a pitch keeps getting turned down and you want a guided run from doubts to rewrite
When you have the pitch and each no, to rank the doubts and get a revised pitch
When the doubts are ranked and both pitch lengths need rewriting around them
When the speaker is sure of the new version, to get the three best arguments against it

tasks.task: Prepare answers for the questions after a talk or pitch

items.when: When the talk has Q&A and the speaker wants short, honest answers ready
When buyers raise the same doubts each time, to give each one an answer with proof
When the answers sound too tidy, to find the hardest questions and the gaps to admit
When the speaker wants a practice grilling before investors or a board

tasks.task: Write remarks for a launch, award or event

items.when: When the remarks are three to five minutes and need one case and one clear ask
When the remarks open a product launch and need one story, a demo and a closing belief
When the occasion is formal, to try a version with a refrain the room can hold on to
When the event is light, to try a deadpan version built on one true story
When the host gives a hard time limit and the remarks run over

tasks.task: Write an all-hands or town hall speech about a change

items.when: When a leader must announce a change and needs the memo, script and listening talks planned
When you need the town hall script, manager talking points and hard-question answers
When the news is a setback, to state the loss, the numbers and the next step plainly
When staff will be angry, to try a version that agrees first and then turns them
Before the meeting, to test the speech against the questions staff will ask

tasks.task: Write a speech for a room that disagrees

items.when: When you know who is in the room and what they believe, to plan a speech that turns them
When the speaker dreads the talk, to map the other side and the easy yeses in order
When the argument is sound but ignores who is listening and what they already hold
When the speech persuades, to mark which lines are fact, guess or opinion
When the draft is done, to find the fair objections it has not answered

tasks.task: Write a fundraising or gala appeal speech

items.when: When the appeal rests on one person's story, to check consent and the facts first
When you have the story and the amount and need remarks that end on one clear ask
When you want a second version with a repeated line donors will remember
When the draft swings between guilt and hope, to hold every line to one feeling

tasks.task: Find the stories and facts a speech will stand on

items.when: When the speech is personal and the speaker has memories but no shape
When the talk is for work, to pick the one case to build on and the surprise under it
When the speaker can talk but not write, to pull raw stories out by asking questions
When the client sends voice memos of their stories and you need them as text
When a long interview must be cut to the few passages worth saying out loud
When the case is a customer's, to list what they must approve before it is told on stage
When the speaker states values and lessons but has no true incident that shows them

tasks.task: Add humour to a speech and check it is safe

items.when: When the speech needs laughs, to plan a deadpan run with the pause and the dropped remark
When the speaker has lessons but no jokes, to get a funny story for each one
When jokes feel forced, to swap them for a few turned lines that are true
When a funny story mocks someone else and should turn on the speaker instead
Before the day, to test each joke against who is in the room

tasks.task: Cut a speech to fit its time slot

items.when: When the speech runs long and must fit without losing the ending or speeding up
When the speech is only a little over, to trim a tenth with every cut logged
When it is far over, to see a version rebuilt around one idea with whole parts removed
After the cut, to time it again at the speaker's real pace

tasks.task: Make cue cards, a delivery copy and a rehearsal plan

items.when: When the words are final and the speaker needs cue cards and a short rehearsal plan
When the speaker wants pace and pause marks written into the script itself
When the speaker wants to hear the speech read aloud before they practise it
After the first timed read, to fix the lines the speaker stumbled on

tasks.task: Write speaker notes and plan slides for a talk

items.when: When the script is done and the speaker needs a storyboard and a deck to match it
When a deck exists and each slide needs notes, transitions and a rehearsal plan
When the speaker wants simple slides with notes that open in any browser
When the speaker wants to see the outline as a draft deck in two or three looks
When the slides repeat the script word for word and add nothing to what is said
When the deck is for a pitch, to check slide count and type size against the talk time

tasks.task: Make a talk work for captions, interpreters and every listener

items.when: When the talk has slides or online viewers and must work for people who cannot see or hear it
When a captioner or interpreter is booked and needs names, terms and the script ahead
When the audience should get a readable handout with private notes left out
When the deck will be shared after, to run an access review and fix what fails
When many listeners use English as a second language and idioms must go

tasks.task: Turn figures and hard ideas into pictures a room can follow

items.when: When the talk has key figures, to turn each into a comparison the room can picture
When an idea is technical, to try an everyday comparison and see where it breaks
When the speaker has a table of numbers and needs the point, the proof and the next step
When a figure sounds striking, to check it against a source before it is said on stage

tasks.task: Write a demo, webinar or video script to be spoken

items.when: When the session is a webinar, to plan one clear result and a teaching outline
When the speaker shows a product live and needs a short script that lets the result speak
When the talk is recorded for video and needs a spoken script with what shows on screen
When the first line on camera matters, to compare openers in five voices with delivery notes
Before recording, to fix every line that trips when spoken

tasks.task: Turn a delivered speech into an article or posts

items.when: When the speaker went off script and you need the words as they were really said
When the speech should become one article that reads well on a page
When you want to see the talk as a blog series, emails, posts and clips before choosing
When the speaker wants one story from the talk as a post under their own name
When spoken repeats and asides must be cleaned up for a reader

always.when: Before any speech with a number, date, award or quoted fact goes to the speaker
Before the delivery copy is printed, to catch names and titles spelt two ways

helpers.when: When the talk needs a designed slide deck, not only notes and a slide plan
When an investor pitch needs the deck, the numbers and the round terms worked out
When a staff speech is one part of a wider change announcement with memos and FAQs
When launch remarks need a press release or media answers to go with them
When the speech must be given or captioned in a second language
When the speech should become a long article, op-ed or chapter under the speaker's name

gaps: No library item writes a wedding speech, best man speech, toast or wedding vows; only the kit covers them
No library item writes a eulogy, obituary or written tribute; the one eulogy item is a life-planning exercise
No library item drafts three different openings or closings for a speech; the hook writers are all for ads and video
No library item writes an award acceptance, thank-you speech or welcome remarks
No library item writes a speaker introduction, a host or MC script, or panel moderator questions
No library item coaches delivery: pace, pauses, nerves or a review of a recorded practice run
No library item lays out cue cards or a teleprompter copy; only the kit's timing and rehearsal plan covers it
No library item checks quotes, poems and song lyrics in a speech for the right source and permission to use
No library item captures one person's speaking voice from samples; the voice items are for brands
No library item prepares a spokesperson for a media interview or press conference
No library item writes a sermon, homily or ceremony script for an officiant
No library item checks a personal speech for tone in a mixed or grieving room beyond the kit's humour check
